title: Aunque, por mucho que, en cuanto: mood after time and concession
summary: Choose indicative or subjunctive after cuando, en cuanto, antes de que, aunque, por mucho que and si bien.
focus: Mood in temporal and concessive clauses
content:
## Time clauses: has it happened yet?

After **cuando**, **en cuanto**, **tan pronto como**, **una vez que**, **hasta que** and **mientras**, the mood depends on whether the event is real yet:

| real (habit or past): indicative | still ahead: subjunctive |
|---|---|
| **Cuando llego** a casa, me ducho. | **Cuando llegues**, llámame. |
| **En cuanto terminó**, se fue. | **En cuanto termine**, te escribo. |
| Esperé **hasta que salió**. | Espera **hasta que salga**. |

Never use the future tense after these words. *Cuando llegarás* is wrong.

## Antes de que and después de que

**Antes de que** always takes the subjunctive, even in the past, because the event had not happened yet at that point:

- *Salimos **antes de que llueva**.* (We'll leave before it rains.)
- *Me fui **antes de que empezara**.* (I left before it started.)

**Después de que** follows the cuando rule: subjunctive for the future (*después de que cenemos*), indicative for the past in careful style (*después de que se fueron*). With one subject, use the infinitive: **antes de salir**, **después de comer**.

## Aunque: a fact or a hypothesis?

| aunque + indicative | aunque + subjunctive |
|---|---|
| **Aunque llueve**, salgo. (It is raining, I know, but I'm going out.) | **Aunque llueva**, salgo. (Even if it rains, I'm going out.) |
| A fact the speaker grants and reports. | A possibility, or a known fact dismissed as irrelevant. |

The second use is subtle. In *Aunque sea tu hermano, no tiene razón*, he **is** your brother, but that changes nothing.

## Stronger concessions

- **por mucho que / por más que** + verb: *Por mucho que insistas, no iré.* With a real, repeated effort the indicative is fine: *Por más que lo intento, no me sale.*
- **por muy** + adjective/adverb + **que** + subjunctive: *Por muy caro que sea…*
- **a pesar de que**, **aun cuando** (formal): these work like aunque.
- **si bien** + indicative (formal writing): *Si bien el plan es caro, merece la pena.*
- **y eso que** + indicative (colloquial afterthought): *Llegó tarde, y eso que salió a las siete.*
- **a pesar de** / **pese a** + noun or infinitive: *pese a la lluvia*, *a pesar de estar cansada*.

vocabulary.meaning: when (indicative for habits and the past, subjunctive for the future)
vocabulary.example: Cuando tengas un rato, revisa este correo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When you have a moment, look over this email.

vocabulary.example: En cuanto sepa algo, te aviso.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As soon as I know anything, I'll let you know.

vocabulary.meaning: as soon as (a little more formal)
vocabulary.example: Tan pronto como recibamos el pago, enviaremos el pedido.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As soon as we receive the payment, we will send the order.

vocabulary.example: Una vez que te acostumbras, el horario es cómodo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Once you get used to it, the timetable is comfortable.

vocabulary.example: No me muevo de aquí hasta que me den una respuesta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm not moving from here until they give me an answer.

vocabulary.example: Guarda la ropa antes de que se ponga a llover.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Bring the washing in before it starts to rain.

vocabulary.example: Hablaremos después de que se vayan los invitados.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We'll talk after the guests leave.

vocabulary.example: Aunque no lo parezca, es muy tímida.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Although it may not look like it, she's very shy.

vocabulary.meaning: however much, no matter how much
vocabulary.example: Por mucho que corras, ya no llegas al tren.
vocabulary.example_meaning: However fast you run, you won't make the train now.

vocabulary.meaning: however (+ adjective or adverb), no matter how
vocabulary.example: Por muy lista que sea, necesita estudiar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: However clever she is, she needs to study.

vocabulary.example: A pesar de que había atasco, llegamos a tiempo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Despite the traffic jam, we arrived on time.

vocabulary.example: Si bien los datos son buenos, conviene ser prudentes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: While the figures are good, it is wise to be cautious.

vocabulary.meaning: and that's despite the fact that (colloquial)
vocabulary.example: Ha suspendido, y eso que estudió todo el fin de semana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He failed, even though he studied all weekend.

vocabulary.meaning: despite, in spite of (+ noun or infinitive)
vocabulary.example: Pese a sus quejas, el jefe no cambió el horario.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Despite their complaints, the boss didn't change the timetable.

quiz.prompt: Tan pronto como ___ los resultados, os los enviaremos.
quiz.explanation: Tan pronto como works like cuando: the results are still ahead, so the present subjunctive follows (tengamos). The future never goes after it, even when the main verb is future.
hints: Do we have the results yet?
The future never follows a time word.

quiz.prompt: En cuanto ___ (terminar, yo) el informe, te lo mando.
quiz.explanation: A future event after en cuanto takes the subjunctive: en cuanto termine.
hints: The report is not finished yet.
Present subjunctive of an -ar verb ends in -e.

quiz.prompt: Nos fuimos antes de que ___ (empezar) a llover.
quiz.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive. In a past sentence it is the imperfect subjunctive: empezara or empezase.
hints: Antes de que never takes the indicative.
The sentence is in the past.

quiz.prompt: What does 'Aunque llueve, salgo a correr' tell you?
options: It is raining, and I'm going for a run anyway.
It might rain, but I'll go for a run anyway.
I'll go for a run as soon as it rains.
quiz.correct_answer: It is raining, and I'm going for a run anyway.
quiz.explanation: Aunque + indicative presents the rain as a fact the speaker knows. 'Even if it rains' would be aunque llueva.

quiz.prompt: Your friend has heard that her new flatmate might be a chef; nobody knows yet. You reply: 'Aunque ___ chef, no pienso dejarle mi cocina.'
quiz.explanation: Nobody knows whether he is a chef, so aunque means 'even if' and takes the subjunctive: aunque sea chef. Es would state it as a known fact.
hints: Is it a known fact, or only a possibility?

quiz.prompt: Por mucho que ___ (insistir, tú), no voy a cambiar de idea.
quiz.explanation: Por mucho que about a possible future insistence takes the subjunctive: insistas.
hints: Will you insist? We don't know yet.
Use the present subjunctive of an -ir verb, tú form.

quiz.prompt: Por ___ cansada que esté, siempre lee un rato antes de dormir.
quiz.explanation: Before an adjective the pattern is por muy + adjective + que, as in por muy cansada que esté (por más cansada que esté is also standard). Mucho does not go before an adjective, and por tan… que is not used.

quiz.prompt: Llegamos tarde, y eso que ___ (salir, nosotros) a las siete.
quiz.explanation: Y eso que adds a real fact as an afterthought, so it takes the indicative: salimos.
hints: It is a fact, told afterwards.

quiz.prompt: ___ el proyecto es caro, sus ventajas son evidentes. (formal report)
quiz.explanation: Si bien + indicative is the formal written way to grant a point before a 'but'. Por mucho que would need a verb of degree and the subjunctive, and hasta que is about time.

listening.text: Avísame en cuanto llegues a casa.
listening.meaning: Let me know as soon as you get home.
listening.note: A future arrival takes the subjunctive.

listening.text: Siempre me llama cuando sale del trabajo.
listening.meaning: She always calls me when she leaves work.

listening.text: Esperaré aquí hasta que termine la reunión.
listening.meaning: I'll wait here until the meeting ends.

listening.text: Aunque está agotada, sigue preparando el examen.
listening.meaning: Although she's exhausted, she keeps preparing for the exam.

listening.text: Por más que lo intento, no me sale la tortilla.
listening.meaning: However hard I try, my omelette doesn't turn out right.
listening.note: A real, repeated effort takes the indicative.

listening.text: Recoge tus cosas antes de que vuelva tu padre.
listening.meaning: Pick up your things before your father comes back.

listening.text: Pese a la niebla, el vuelo despegó a su hora.
listening.meaning: Despite the fog, the flight took off on time.
listening.note: New word: la niebla = the fog.

listening.text: Una vez que hayas firmado el contrato, ya no podrás echarte atrás.
listening.meaning: Once you have signed the contract, you won't be able to back out.
listening.note: New word: echarse atrás = to back out.

guide.tip: Ask one question. Has it happened yet, or does it happen regularly? Then use the indicative. Is it still ahead? Then use the subjunctive.

conversations.title: Moving to Lisbon
conversations.scenario: Lucía tells her friend Andrés she has accepted a job abroad; he tries to talk her out of it.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me han ofrecido el puesto en Lisboa y he dicho que sí.
lines.meaning: They offered me the job in Lisbon and I said yes.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Seriously? And when are you leaving?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: En cuanto termine el curso, a finales de junio.
lines.meaning: As soon as the course finishes, at the end of June.
lines.note: A future event: en cuanto takes the subjunctive.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Aunque te paguen el doble, vas a echar de menos a todo el mundo.
lines.meaning: Even if they pay you double, you're going to miss everyone.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ya lo sé, y eso que todavía no me he ido.
lines.meaning: I know, and I haven't even left yet.
lines.note: Y eso que + indicative gives a real fact as an afterthought.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Por mucho que me lo expliques, no lo entiendo.
lines.meaning: However much you explain it to me, I don't get it.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Si bien el sueldo es mejor, lo que me atrae es el proyecto.
lines.meaning: While the salary is better, what attracts me is the project.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Bueno, prométeme que vendrás antes de que llegue el invierno.
lines.meaning: Well, promise me you'll come back before winter arrives.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Te lo prometo. Y cuando venga, cenamos en nuestro bar de siempre.
lines.meaning: I promise. And when I come, we'll have dinner at our usual bar.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Hecho. Pero no te pongas sentimental hasta que no hagas la maleta.
lines.meaning: Deal. But don't get sentimental until you've packed your suitcase.
lines.note: Colloquial hasta que no: the no adds nothing.

bites.title: Still ahead? Subjunctive
bites.rule: After cuando, en cuanto, hasta que or una vez que, use the indicative for habits and the past and the subjunctive for the future. Never use the future tense.

bites.title: Antes de que: always subjunctive
bites.rule: Antes de que takes the subjunctive even in the past, because the event had not happened yet. Same subject? Use antes de + infinitive.
bites.example: Me fui antes de que empezara la película.
bites.example_meaning: I left before the film started.

bites.title: Aunque: fact or 'even if'
bites.rule: Aunque + indicative reports a fact. Aunque + subjunctive is 'even if', or a known fact brushed aside as irrelevant.
bites.example: Aunque sea tu jefe, no tiene razón.
bites.example_meaning: He may be your boss, but he's not right.

bites.title: Por mucho que, por muy… que
bites.rule: Por mucho/más que + verb, por muy + adjective + que: 'no matter how'. Use the subjunctive for the hypothetical. Si bien and y eso que take the indicative.
bites.example: Por muy tarde que sea, llámame.
bites.example_meaning: However late it is, call me.

sorts.title: Which mood after the time word?

items.text: Cuando salgo del trabajo, voy al gimnasio.
Cuando salgas del trabajo, ven a verme.
En cuanto llegó, se puso a cocinar.
En cuanto llegue, se pondrá a cocinar.
Esperamos hasta que abrieron la puerta.
Esperaremos hasta que abran la puerta.

sorts.why: The same connector takes the indicative for something real (a habit or a past event) and the subjunctive for something still to come.

sorts.title: Aunque: what does the speaker mean?

items.text: Aunque hace frío, no llevo abrigo.
Aunque haga frío, no llevaré abrigo.
Aunque es caro, lo voy a comprar.
Aunque sea caro, lo voy a comprar.
Si bien el plan tiene riesgos, es el mejor.
Por mucho que protestes, no cambiará nada.

sorts.why: The indicative presents the concession as information. The subjunctive leaves it open or dismisses it.

spots.why: A future event after cuando takes the present subjunctive, never the future.

spots.sentence: Salimos antes de que empieza el partido.
spots.why: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Te espero hasta que terminas los deberes.
spots.why: The homework is not finished yet, so hasta que takes the subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Por mucho rápido que corras, no llegarás.
spots.why: Before an adjective or adverb the pattern is por muy … que.

spots.sentence: Si bien sea caro, merece la pena.
spots.why: Si bien grants a fact and takes the indicative.

builds.text: Llámame en cuanto llegues a casa.
builds.meaning: Call me as soon as you get home.
We'll leave before it gets dark.

builds.text: Por muy tarde que sea, llámame.
builds.meaning: However late it is, call me.

builds.text: Aunque llueva, iremos a la playa.
builds.meaning: Even if it rains, we'll go to the beach.
